title: Phased Embedding Model Swaps with Quality Guards and Autoscale-aware Rollouts
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: We are onboarding multiple new embedding model families (float and quantized variants) and need a safe, observable path to swap models used by embeddings and reranking endpoints without regressing quality or violating latency SLOs. This ticket defines a phased swap + rollback policy that is autoscale-aware and integrates with Console dashboards and Optimize recommendations.

Goals: 
- Allow traffic-split canaries for embedding model versions with automatic metric gating.
- Protect reranking by validating downstream reranker score distributions and pairwise rank stability during canaries.
- Ensure autoscaling and batching configurations adapt during rollouts so we don't spike per-token cost or latency.
- Provide a reproducible rollback/playbook and automated partial-rollout tooling.
- Document deprecation timeline and data migration plan for stored vectors.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Traffic-split API (internal) supports deterministic version tags: e.g., model:embed-family@vX.Y.Z and can route by percentage to variants.
2) Canary guard rails implemented: A/B metrics evaluated every 10m (embedding cosine drift, reranker NDCG@10 delta, p50/p95 latency). Thresholds configurable per-project.
3) Console shows per-route embedding-model heatmap and an automated alert when canary breaches threshold.
4) Autoscaler policy adapts: when canary traffic is enabled, autoscaling multiplier reduces warm-up to avoid cold-start latency spikes and KV cache warming is prioritized for canary buckets.
5) Playbook with rollback procedures, client compatibility checks, and vector migration steps committed to docs.
6) End-to-end experiment performed with internal customer (Search Team) and results recorded.

Technical approach: 
- Versioning: enforce semantic model tags and canonical metadata in model-catalog service. Each model upload must include 'embedding_schema' fingerprint and a stable tokenizer hash.
- Routing: extend the embed-gateway to accept a stable 'model_version' header and a 'traffic_split' config stored per-project. Traffic splitting uses deterministic hashing by request id to avoid correlated KV cache churn.
- Canary metrics: implement a lightweight evaluation pipeline that samples 0.5% of production requests for embedding pair comparisons and reranker scoring; compute rolling statistics and publish to metrics store.
- Quality gates: NDCG regression >= -0.01 absolute or cosine drift <= 0.03 (default thresholds) will mark canary as failed. Gates are configurable per-project via Console.
- KV cache warming: when promoting a new model variant to canary, precompute top-1k prefixes for the affected routes using background jobs to reduce early latency.
- Autoscale-aware rollout: add a 'rollout_mode' flag (gradual | static | burst) to deployment config. For gradual mode, autoscaler will use predicted token-per-second from historical distribution and allocate headroom to prevent cold-start.
- Vector storage: provide a live re-embedding job template that supports batched re-compute and index swap with low-lock semantics; expose progress in Console.
- Rollback: automated circuit that flips traffic_split back to previous version and marks latest model as deprecated; run reverse KV migration to invalidate warmed cache for failed model.

Risks and trade-offs: 
- Sampling adds overhead to metrics pipeline; keep sample small and use async processing.
- Deterministic hashing for traffic split may reduce randomness of exposure; acceptable to reduce KV churn.
- Pre-warming increases temporary cost; we cap warming jobs and track ROI via Optimize.

Artifacts and links: 
- Design doc: https://company-confluence.internal/redwood/embeddings/phased-swap-design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/embed-gateway/pull/1123
- Canary metrics dashboard: https://console.redwood/s/dashboards/embeds-canary
- Reembedding job template: https://drive.redwood.com/embeddings/recompute-template.xlsx

Implementation plan (milestones): 
1) Schema & model-catalog enforcement (ENG-33810) 
2) Routing + deterministic hashing and traffic-split API (this ticket) 
3) Canary metrics pipeline & default gates (ENG-33845) 
4) KV pre-warm job + autoscaler hooks (ENG-33902) 
5) Console UI for gates + rollout controls (PM + DX work) 
6) Run first internal canary and iterate on thresholds

Notes: This ticket coordinates closely with Console (PM: Lena Cho), Runtime autoscaler (ENG: Omar Singh), and Search team for a pilot.
